candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — administer and titrate IV medications safely, monitor therapeutic/adverse effects, and respond to medication-related hemodynamic changes
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — IV esmolol titration and hypotension
candidate.educational_objective: Use esmolol's very short half-life safely by promptly reducing or stopping the infusion for unacceptable hypotension while continuing close blood-pressure, heart-rate, and rhythm monitoring.

options.A: Reduce or stop the esmolol infusion and continue close hemodynamic monitoring because its very short elimination half-life allows the beta-blocking effect to decrease quickly after the infusion is changed.
options.B: Continue the same infusion rate because esmolol has a prolonged half-life and hypotension will not improve after dose reduction.
options.C: Increase the infusion rate because hypotension indicates inadequate beta blockade.
options.D: Discontinue hemodynamic monitoring after stopping the infusion because esmolol cannot cause bradycardia or recurrent cardiovascular effects.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current FDA/DailyMed labeling states that esmolol has an elimination half-life of about 9 minutes, that blood levels can be rapidly changed by adjusting the infusion rate, and that hypotension should prompt dose reduction or discontinuation. The label also requires close monitoring for hypotension, heart rate, and rhythm because clinically important hypotension and bradycardia can occur. B reverses esmolol's pharmacokinetic advantage. C would worsen dose-related hypotension. D is unsafe because cardiovascular monitoring remains necessary while the clinical response is reassessed.
candidate.source_claim_supported: IV esmolol has an approximately 9-minute elimination half-life and can be rapidly titrated; unacceptable hypotension or severe bradycardia should prompt reduction or discontinuation with continued close hemodynamic monitoring.
candidate.source_locator: Warnings and Precautions, Sections 5.1 Hypotension and 5.2 Bradycardia — monitor closely; reduce or stop for unacceptable hypotension or severe bradycardia. Clinical Pharmacology, Sections 12.1 and 12.3 — elimination half-life approximately 9 minutes; blood levels can be rapidly altered by infusion-rate changes and fall rapidly after termination

candidate.stem: A client receiving an IV esmolol infusion for rapid ventricular rate develops an unacceptable drop in blood pressure. Which nursing action is most appropriate?
